info.description:
Public API for Indian primary law: Central and State Acts, the instruments of the principal regulators, and their individual sections. Also the Anuvad translation API, which translates legal documents between English and the 22 languages of the Eighth Schedule. This document is the India surface only; US statutes are a separate document at `/external/openapi.json`.

**Authentication**: Pass your API key as `Authorization: Bearer vq_key_...` (preferred) or in the `X-API-Key` header. The `api_key` query parameter also works where a header cannot be set, but a URL ends up in logs and browser history. Sending two different keys in one request is rejected with a 401. The same key works against the US API; the two share one credit balance.

**Credits**: Each primary-law call costs API credits. See `GET /api/v1/api-credits/pricing` for the full pricing matrix. The `/translation/*` routes are the exception: they bill PAGES from a separate pool sold in INR, not credits. See the Translation API tag.

## Coverage

Central, State and Union Territory enactments, addressable down to the individual section, plus the instruments of the principal regulators. Regulators covered include SEBI, RBI, MCA, IRDAI, TRAI, DGFT, MOEFCC and CPCB.

`GET /acts/filters` is free and returns the live section count behind every `category`, `state` and `department` value, so read volumes from there rather than from this page.

`sourceUrl` points at the publisher's own document where we hold a live one, and is `null` otherwise (India Code re-minted its identifiers in August 2026, so we return nothing rather than a link that 404s). `pdfUrl` and `textUrl` are served from our own mirror.

get.description:
Section-by-section mapping from a repealed Indian criminal code to the 2023
code that replaced it, in force from 1 July 2024.

Pass either side of the pair: `ipc` and `bns` both return the IPC to BNS
mapping, `crpc` and `bnss` both return CrPC to BNSS.

**Coverage**: `ipc`/`bns` and `crpc`/`bnss`. `iea`/`bsa` are accepted but
return 404 until the Evidence Act mapping lands, rather than an empty list
that would read as "nothing changed".

**One section, not the whole table.** Without a filter the answer is the whole
table. Pass `section` (a section of the REPEALED
code, such as `302` for the IPC) and/or `newSection` (a section of the
successor, such as `103` for the BNS); when both are given a row must match
both. Matching is exact on the section number after case and spaces are folded
(`498A`, `498a` and `498 a` are the same), so `30` never reaches `302`. A
filter with no bracket also reaches that section's sub-provisions: the BNS side
is stored as `103(1)`, so `newSection=103` returns every `103(n)` row, while
`newSection=103(1)` returns only that one. `section` always means the repealed
code and `newSection` its successor, whichever side you put in the path. A
filter that matches nothing is a 200 with an empty `provisions` list and a
`note`, never a 404: it does not mean the section is unchanged. The price is the
same with or without a filter.

**Source**: transcribed from the correspondence tables published by the Bureau
of Police Research and Development, an attached office of India's Ministry of
Home Affairs. The `coverage.source` block on every response names the exact
document and links to it.

**Both codes are live law at once.** The repealed code still governs offences
committed before 1 July 2024, for the lifetime of pending trials, so this is a
correspondence and not a redirect.

**Authentication**: API key via `Authorization: Bearer vq_key_...`

**Cost**: 1 credit

get.description:
Describe the corpus behind this API: how many acts and provisions it holds, how
they break down by jurisdiction, regulator and status, and how DEEP that holding
goes.

**Cost: free.**

Read the `depth` block before building on this API. It answers four independent
questions, because "we hold the act" and "we hold what amended it" are different
claims and only one of them is true for most of the corpus:

- `actsWithText` is every act we serve;
- `actsWithAmendmentEvents` is the much smaller set for which we hold parsed
  amendment records;
- `actsClaimingAmendmentsWithoutEvents` is the known gap between them, published
  so that an empty amendment list is legible as a gap rather than as a claim
  that nothing ever changed.

Two different kinds of count appear here and they are labelled. `passages` in
the breakdown lists is faceted live and exact right now. `totals.acts`,
`totals.actsRetired` and `totals.sections` follow the act index that the weekly
sync republishes (`totals.totalsSource` says so, and `totals.measuredOn` is the
index's generation date). The `depth` counts need a full distinct-act scan that
cannot run inside a request, so they are dated: see `depth.depthMeasuredOn`. Do
not divide passages into the act-level counts.

`meta.sourceCheckedAt` says when the weekly sync last compared the publisher
with the corpus, and `meta.corpusRefreshedAt` when it last finished writing
changes. Null means the sync has not recorded it yet.

**`include=filters`** adds `data.filters`: the exact payload `GET /acts/filters`
returns (`categories`, `states`, `departments`, `truncated`), built by the same
function from the same one-hour cache that `POST /acts/search` validates its
filter values against. Read `data.filters.truncated` before concluding a value
is not valid: a field named there is a partial list. Without `include`, the
response has no `filters` key. An unrecognised `include` value is a 422.

get.description:
Turn a citation a lawyer would type into the provision it names.

Cost: 2 credits. A malformed citation is a 422 and is not charged. Every other
outcome is, including `not_found`: a confident negative is the answer.

Accepts what Indian practice writes, not what a style guide prescribes: element
order does not matter and the common `u/s 302 IPC` form works. All of these
resolve:

    u/s 302 IPC
    Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860
    s.302 IPC
    S. 376(2)(g), IPC
    clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 302 IPC
    O. 39 R. 1 CPC
    Art. 21 of the Constitution
    Regulation 24 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015
    Maharashtra Act No. LXXVII of 2018

Read `status` before `candidates`. `ambiguous` is a real answer and is charged.
The commonest cause is the 2023 recodification: after 1 July 2024, `s. 302`
names both IPC 302 (murder) and BNS 302 (uttering words to wound religious
feelings), while BNS 103 is murder. Both codes stay live for pending trials, so
the endpoint will not choose for you until you send `asAtDate`. The other
code's section is looked up in the correspondence table, never assumed to be the
same number: `s 302 IPC` pairs with BNS 103. With `asAtDate`, a date before
2024-07-01 returns the old code and a date on or after it returns the new one.
The IPC, CrPC and Indian Evidence Act are reported as repealed from that date,
with the replacing code named in `note`. A central act is preferred over a State
copy of the same title unless you send `state`.

`r/w` ("read with") is split into separate citations and each is resolved.

get.description:
The publisher's own text for one provision.

**Cost: 3 credits.** Refunded when we hold the provision and cannot reproduce
its text, because you asked for text and did not get it.

The text is sliced out of the act document by the character offsets stored with
each passage. It is never assembled by concatenating search passages: those
carry a retrieval header that we synthesized (`Act: ... | India | State | In
Force`), and serving that as statute would put our words inside a quotation of
the law.

`?version=<versionId>` returns the text as it stood in a stored version (list
them with `GET /acts/{actId}/versions`), rebuilt from that version's stored
passages, with a `version` block. An unknown version is a 404 with
`reason: version_not_found` and is refunded. Observed dates are when the weekly sync saw the publisher's
text, not legal effective dates.

A provision whose text cannot be shown to be that provision is not served. The
stored offsets are checked against the passage text we hold, a passage that
opens with another section's heading or sits in an Objects and Reasons note is
refused, and passages that only share the section number (a schedule item, a
footnote) are left out. Then `available` is false, `bodyProvenance.integrity`
names the reason, and the call is refunded.

**This text is as the publisher published it.** We do not apply amendments to
it. `GET /acts/{actId}/sections/{n}/history` lists every amendment we hold for
the provision, each with an `appliedStatus` saying whether it is reflected here.
It is not.

The amendment record for a single provision: what changed, which Act changed it,
which of that Act's sections did so, when it took effect where the publisher

then, how many had not, and how many carry no date. `isBounded` true means no
recorded event affects that date, which is not the same as there having been
none.

footnote behind it, and about half the records held carry no effective date. Read

get.description:
The act-level change feed of the weekly corpus sync: which acts were newly
loaded, had their text replaced, or had their amendment record or metadata
updated, run by run, oldest first.

**Cost: 1 credit.** Refunded when the feed cannot be read, and when no run has
published one yet.

Page with `cursor`: pass the `nextCursor` of one page as the `cursor` of the
next, unchanged. Store the last one you processed and you will see every change
exactly once. `since` (YYYY-MM-DD) starts the feed at the first run swept on or
after that date, and is day-granular.

To POLL, keep `resumeCursor` rather than `since`. At the head of the feed
`nextCursor` is null and `hasMore` false, but `resumeCursor` is still set: send
it as `cursor` on the next poll and you get an empty page until a newer sweep
lands, then only the rows of that sweep. Re-sending `since=<date>` instead
re-delivers the whole of the last run, which you would have to dedupe on
(`runId`, `actId`, `versionId`).

Each `changes` row carries the act's `versionId` after the change; read the
prior text with `GET /acts/{actId}/versions` and `?version=`.

**One act.** Pass `actId` to keep only that act's rows. Order, `cursor`, `since`
and `resumeCursor` work exactly as above, and a cursor from the unfiltered feed
is accepted. `withdrawnCandidates` is always empty under `actId`, because those
items carry no act id. An id that is well formed but has no row in the window
returns an empty page with a `note`, which is not a statement that the act does
not exist; an id that can never be one (it contains a slash, or spaces inside)
is a 422 that costs nothing. The filter reads every run in the window, so pass
`since` when the feed is long. This is the act's change EVENTS (runs and
sweeps, including `amendments` and `metadata`). For the act's stored VERSIONS
(content hash, passage count, observed end date) use `GET /acts/{actId}/versions`.

`withdrawnCandidates` are items the publisher no longer lists. They are
reported, never applied: the act is still served until a person decides.

Dates are when the sync observed the publisher's text, not legal effective
dates.

Returns the translation and OCR pages this API key's account can spend now.

**Free.** Never charged, so you can poll it to drive alerting or a pre-flight
check without the check itself costing you anything. Like the credit balance,
it is designed to still answer when the answer is "nothing": at a zero balance
a metered call 402s and tells you nothing, which is the moment the number
matters most.

**Authentication:** a `vq_key_` key holding `translate:read`.

## Pages, not characters

This product bills physical pages. A page of text is 2,000 characters; a page
of a document is a page of that document. Nothing here is counted in tokens.

## Two pools, and which one this API spends

`translation` and `ocr` are separate balances, not two views of one number.

**Translating a document, scanned or not, spends translation pages only.**
Reading a scan is included in that price: this API does not charge you OCR
pages for it. Budget from the `translation` pool.

The `ocr` pool exists for standalone text extraction, which is a separate
operation this API surface does not currently expose. It is reported here so
the figure is visible to an account that holds OCR pages, not because a
translation call will draw on it.

## Your free allowance applies here too

Pages are pooled per ACCOUNT, not per credential, so the monthly free allowance
your account holds is spendable through the API as well. A charge draws on
`free` before `paid`, which means the first pages of a month can cost nothing
and leave `paid` untouched.

Budget from `pagesRemaining`, which is `free` plus `paid`. Budgeting from `paid`
alone understates what you can spend.

## Separate from API credits

Translation pages and API credits are different currencies on different
ledgers. `GET /credits/balance` reports credits for the primary-law endpoints
and says nothing about pages; this endpoint reports pages and says nothing
about credits. Neither pays for the other.

## Pages are pooled per organization

If your key belongs to an organization, these figures are the ORGANIZATION's
pooled balance, not your personal one. Every member spends from the same pool,
so a colleague's large job changes what you see here.

## Example

```bash
curl https://api.vaquill.ai/api/v1/in/translation/balance \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VAQUILL_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "translation": {
    "pagesRemaining": 1480,
    "free": 0,
    "paid": 1480,
    "totalPurchased": 2000,
    "totalConsumed": 520
  },
  "ocr": {
    "pagesRemaining": 310,
    "free": 0,
    "paid": 310,
    "totalPurchased": 500,
    "totalConsumed": 190
  },
  "pagesArePhysical": true,
  "asOf": "2026-11-01T12:34:56Z"
}
```

post.description:
Starts translating a file you uploaded with `POST /in/translation/files`.

**Charged in pages, when the translation finishes.** Submitting costs nothing.
The job spends one translation page per physical page of the document, once, on
completion, and a job that fails spends nothing.

**Authentication:** a `vq_key_` key holding `translate:write`. A wildcard (`*`)
key includes it.

## Asynchronous

You get `202 Accepted`, a `documentId` and a `Location` header. Poll
`GET /in/translation/documents/{id}` until `status` is `completed` (or `failed`),
then download with `GET /in/translation/documents/{id}/content`. Documents take
from seconds to several minutes depending on length.

## What is checked before the job is queued

Everything refusable is refused before anything is queued: an unsupported
language (read `GET /in/translation/languages`), an unknown `outputFormat`,
`courtStyle` or `engine`, an unknown or foreign `fileId` (404) and an
insufficient balance (402).

The balance check uses the page count recorded at upload. For `pdf` and `docx`
that is exact. For images and plain text the count is not known until the job
runs, so the check only confirms you hold at least one page; if the real count
is higher than your balance the job ends `failed` with
`INSUFFICIENT_TRANSLATION_PAGES` and you are not charged.

Reading a scanned document is included in those translation pages: this route
never spends pages from the separate OCR pool.

## Formatting the output

`courtStyle` renders the translation to an Indian court's mandated paper, font,
margins and line spacing (Supreme Court and nine High Courts). Omit it for the
compact reader-friendly layout, which is about 45% fewer pages. The font mandate
applies when `targetLanguage` is English; an Indic target is always set in Noto
Sans, because the mandated Latin faces carry no Devanagari, while paper size,
margins and spacing still apply.

Tables, figures and document structure are preserved on every job. That is the
default path, not an option, so there is no flag to set.

`handwritten: true` routes extraction through a vision model that reads
handwriting far better than the default OCR, at a higher cost per page to us.
Page billing is unchanged either way. Leave it false for born-digital or clean
typed documents, where the default is both cheaper and as accurate.

`engine` selects the translation model: omit it for `gpt54` (recommended),
`gpt54mini` for cheaper and faster work on simple text, `sarvam` for Indic
languages. Billing does not change with the engine.

## Removing stamps and signatures

Stamp, seal and signature images can be dropped from the rendered output. This
is an ACCOUNT setting rather than a per-job field, so it applies to every job
this account submits, through the API and the web app alike. Set it once in your
Anuvad profile and this route honours it. Images are classified and only removed
above a confidence threshold, so an unclear mark is kept rather than guessed
away.

## No URLs

This route does not accept a URL, only a `fileId`. A `sourceFileUrl` field is
a 422.

## Duplicates

Submitting the same `fileId` with the same languages and format again while the
first job is still running returns that job (still `202`) instead of starting a
second one. Once it has finished, the same request starts a new job.

get.description:
Returns the status of a document translation job.

**Free.** Never charged, so poll as often as the rate limit allows. A sensible
cadence is every 2 to 5 seconds.

**Authentication:** a `vq_key_` key holding `translate:read`.

## Status

| `status` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `pending` | Queued, not started. |
| `processing` | Being translated. `progress` runs from 0 to 100. |
| `completed` | Done. Download it from `/content`. `pagesCharged` is set. |
| `failed` | Not translated and not charged. See `error.code`. |

`pagesCharged` is `null` until the job completes, because pages are charged
once, on completion.

## Errors

`error.code` is `INSUFFICIENT_TRANSLATION_PAGES` (your balance did not cover the
document when it was processed) or `TRANSLATION_FAILED`. Neither charges you.

## Example

```bash
curl https://api.vaquill.ai/api/v1/in/translation/documents/$DOCUMENT_ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VAQUILL_API_KEY"
```

get.description:
Downloads the translated file once the job has completed.

**Free.** Never charged, and downloading again never charges again.

**Authentication:** a `vq_key_` key holding `translate:read`.

## Bytes, not a link

The file is streamed through this API. The response body IS the file: there is
no URL to follow, nothing that expires, and nothing to forward. Send the same
`Authorization` header you use for every other call.

## Which file you get

By default, the format you asked for in `outputFormat`. A job submitted with
`outputFormat=pdf` also produces a Word copy when one could be generated; add
`?format=docx` to download it. `?format=pdf` asks for the PDF explicitly. If the
format you ask for does not exist for this job the answer is 404.

`Content-Type` and `Content-Disposition` (an attachment with a filename) are set
from the file. `ETag` is supported (`If-None-Match` gives `304`) and so is
`Range` (`206`) for plain, unencrypted files, so an interrupted download can
resume.

## Not finished

While `status` is not `completed` this is a 404. Poll the status route first.

## Example

```bash
curl -o translated.pdf \
  https://api.vaquill.ai/api/v1/in/translation/documents/$DOCUMENT_ID/content \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VAQUILL_API_KEY"
```

post.description:
Uploads a source file and returns a `fileId` to translate it with.

**Free.** Never charged: pages are spent when a translation finishes, not on
upload or retrieval, so a file you never translate costs nothing.

**Authentication:** a `vq_key_` key holding `translate:write`. A wildcard (`*`)
key includes it.

## Why this route exists

`POST /in/translation/documents` does not accept a URL. It accepts the `fileId`
returned here, which refers to a file this API stored for your account. That is
deliberate: the API never fetches an address you name, so it cannot be pointed
at an internal service or at someone else's document. A `fileId` from another
account is a 404.

## Limits

- Types: `pdf`, `docx`, `txt`, `jpg`, `jpeg`, `png`, `tif`, `tiff`, `webp`, `bmp`.
- Size: at most 150 MB, and not empty.
- A `fileId` is valid for 24 hours. You can translate one file into several
  languages by posting `/documents` more than once with the same `fileId`.

## `pageCount`

Physical pages for `pdf` and `docx`, which is what you will be charged. For
images and plain text it is `null`: their page count is only known when the job
runs, and `POST /documents` can then only check you hold at least one page.

## Example

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.vaquill.ai/api/v1/in/translation/files \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VAQUILL_API_KEY" \
  -F "file=@petition.pdf"
```

get.description:
Returns every language this API can translate from and to.

**Free.** Never charged, so you can call it at start-up or on a schedule to
keep your own list current. It is rate limited like every other
key-authenticated route.

**Authentication:** a `vq_key_` key holding `translate:read`.

## Read this instead of hard-coding the list

A code you invent is refused with a 422 before any page is charged, and the
error names what is supported. Reading the list means a language we add works
on your side with no change, and it means you never pay to discover a typo.

Regional tags are accepted and narrowed to the language, so `hi-IN` is read as
`hi`. You do not need to strip them yourself.

## Scope

English plus the 22 languages of the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution of
India. These are the languages Indian courts and governments work in, and each
one is backed by script support in rendered output.

`auto` appears in this list as a SOURCE only. There is no translating into an
undetermined language, so sending it as `targetLanguage` is a 422 that says so.

## Direction is not decoration

`direction` is `rtl` for Urdu, Sindhi and Kashmiri. Honour it when you render
a language's own name and when you display translated output, or a correct
translation is shown wrongly.

## Example

```bash
curl https://api.vaquill.ai/api/v1/in/translation/languages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VAQUILL_API_KEY"
```

unit the payment is charged in. `priceInr` is GST-inclusive and is the amount
you pay. Only `pricePerPageInr` is in rupees, and it is a display figure.

Read this list rather than hard-coding a price. Larger packs are cheaper per
page, and both pools (`translation` and `ocr`) have their own packs.

post.description:
Translates a piece of text and returns it in the same response.

**Charged in pages.** See the cost rules below. A failed translation is
refunded in full.

**Authentication:** a `vq_key_` key holding `translate:write`. A wildcard (`*`)
key includes it.

## Pages, not characters

This product bills pages. A page of text is 2,000 characters, and the cost is
`ceil(characters / 2000)`.

| Characters | Pages |
| --- | --- |
| 1 to 2,000 | 1 |
| 2,001 to 4,000 | 2 |
| 50,000 | 25 |

**Any non-empty text costs at least 1 page.** Unlike the dashboard, there is no
free floor on SIZE here: a 10-character request spends a page. Empty or
whitespace-only text is a 422 and costs nothing.

**The one free case:** a `sourceLanguage` you name explicitly that equals
`targetLanguage` (for example `en` to `en`). Nothing is translated, the text
comes back as sent, and `pagesCharged` is 0. With `sourceLanguage` left at
`auto` the text is always translated and charged, because the detected
language may differ from what you expect.

That is about size, not about your allowance. Your account's monthly free pages
are spendable through the API, and a charge draws on them first, so a short
request can still cost you nothing out of pocket.

## When you are charged and when you are not

Everything that can be checked up front is checked BEFORE the charge, and a
refusal costs nothing: an unsupported language (read `GET /in/translation/languages`
instead of hard-coding it), text over 50,000 characters (a 422, never a
truncation) and empty text.

If your balance cannot cover the pages you get a 402 and nothing is translated.

Once charged, if the translation fails or comes back empty the pages are
refunded and you get an error. You are never billed for a translation you did
not receive.

## Retries

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header. A retry of the same request with the same key
returns the original response and does not charge again.

## Limits

Text is at most 50,000 characters, because this route holds the connection open
while the translation runs. Anything longer belongs on the document routes.

## Example

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.vaquill.ai/api/v1/in/translation/translations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VAQUILL_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text": "The petitioner submits that the impugned order is contrary to law.", "targetLanguage": "hi", "sourceLanguage": "en"}'
```

```json
{
  "translatedText": "याचिकाकर्ता का निवेदन है कि आक्षेपित आदेश विधि के विरुद्ध है।",
  "detectedLanguage": "en",
  "targetLanguage": "hi",
  "pagesCharged": 1,
  "charCount": 66
}
```

get.description:
The fifteen forums whose matters we hold, each with its record count, the span of decisions, how
many of its matters are judgments, and how many of its documents we actually have.

**Free.** Call it first: it carries the `code` every other route on this surface takes.

Four of the fifteen entries are not tribunals. The CCI is a regulator, the IBBI a board, RERA an
authority and the GST AAR an advance-ruling body; `forumType` says which is which, and the path
is `/tribunals` for all of them because splitting it would mean a caller has to know a body's
constitutional character before they can look up a matter.

`recordCount` is live from the publisher's own statistics table for the forums that have a row
there, and our measured figure, with `countedAt` null, for the forums that do not. If that table
cannot be read at all this endpoint answers `503` rather than serving the measured figures as if
they were live. `files` is per forum on purpose:
document coverage ranges from complete to 43% missing depending on the forum, so one
corpus-wide number would mislead every caller it reached.

400.description: `unknown_tribunal`, `invalid_query` (including a search or `caseNumber` filter sent without `tribunal`) or `invalid_cursor`. Not charged: every one of these is decided before the credit is consumed.

503.description: `tribunals_backend_unavailable`: a backend failed or timed out. Refunded. The only status on this surface worth retrying.

get.description:
Matters by forum, bench, year, decision date or exact case number, newest decision first, paged
with a cursor.

**Cost: 1 credit per page.** Refunded when a backend fails. An unknown forum, a contradictory
filter or a bad cursor is refused for free, before the charge.

There is deliberately **no `total`**: counting 813,168 rows per request to produce a number
nobody pages to the end of is the defect this surface's sibling was built to avoid. Use
`hasMore` and `nextCursor`, and `GET /forums` for per-forum counts.

Order is `decisionDate` descending, then `caseId`, with undated matters last. **Do not sort on
`scrapedAt`**: it is when we collected the record, not when the matter was decided, and APTEL
matters decided in 2011 are all stamped 2026-03-13.

`caseNumber` matches exactly. It is not a free-text target: there is no index supporting a
substring match on it, so the term search covers `title`, `petitioner` and `respondent` instead.
**`caseNumber` needs a `tribunal`.** Unscoped it scans every forum and either took about 7 seconds
or failed with a 503, so it is refused up front with a 400 `invalid_query` that is not charged. With
`tribunal` it answers in about a second.

get.description:
The individual orders a forum recorded against one matter, newest first. A truncated list
drops the oldest.

**Cost: 1 credit.** Refunded when no such matter exists or a backend fails.

**Only three of the fifteen forums keep an order list** (`hasOrderList` on `GET /forums` says

`status: not_applicable` and an empty list. That is an answer, not an error: the matter exists

`status` is the field to read before the list:

- `listed`: the lookup ran. `orders` is the result, and may legitimately be empty.
- `not_applicable`: this forum publishes no order list.

`truncated` is `true` when the list is shorter than what the forum holds, and `omitted` says by
how many where the forum reports a count. NCLT's history keeps the final orders only, so a matter
whose `forumAttributes.orderCount` is 6 can list 1 order with `truncated: true, omitted: 5`.

`GET /matters/{tribunal}/{caseId}/orders/{index}/file` with this list's `index`. `GET /file` stays
the one document held for the matter, in every forum, so that "the file" never silently means

**This product bills PAGES, not credits, characters or tokens.** A page of text is 2,000 characters; a page of a document is a physical page. Translation pages and OCR pages are SEPARATE pools, and these routes spend TRANSLATION pages only. Reading a scanned document is included in the document price: this API does not charge OCR pages for it.

Pages are a different currency from the API credits every other endpoint in this document uses. Neither pays for the other, and `GET /api/v1/in/translation/balance` reports pages while `GET /api/v1/in/credits/balance` reports credits.
